**Finding submitted: `needs_review` (no redline).**

Summary of the investigation:

- **The rule has no target in this document.** This is an ABS Transfer and Servicing Agreement between the Trust/Depositor (us) and Cellco as Servicer/Marketing Agent. Cellco does not license us any software, product or IP, so there is no grant clause whose scope, revocability, term or transferability could be measured against the preferred or fallback positions.
- **Full-text verification:** every `Grant`/`Granted` hit is a security-interest grant in the Depositor Transferred Property (p0048, p0067, and the defined term at p0763); every `license` hit other than p0346 is a due-qualification representation about regulatory licences (p0234, p0259, p0272). Searches for `intellectual property`, `trademark`, `royalty-free`, `irrevocable`, `proprietary` and `right to use` returned nothing relevant, and the A-1–A-41 sections are just the definitions annex.
- **Why not "missing":** "missing" implies the rule expects a clause that was omitted. Here the absence is structural to the deal type, not a drafting gap — writing a licence grant into a receivables securitisation would not fit the instrument. That is a scoping call for the reviewing team, hence needs_review.

One substantive point I deliberately did **not** redline: Section 7.5(b) (p0346) is the mirror image of this rule — it expressly negates any obligation for the Servicer to license or assign its processes, models or servicing software to a Successor Servicer, leaving no path to the servicing platform on a transition. That is a real continuity exposure, but it is the identical commercial term the TRANSITION rule covers (as the planner flagged), so per the no-double-flagging instruction I noted it in the rationale and deferred it. I also noted that Section 7.6 (p0348) confers succession rights on the *Servicer*, which benefits the counterparty and falls outside this rule's direction.
